name: Ethereum
thesis: Price sits at the bottom of its 30-day range after a 16.1% monthly fall. ETH trades at 3071.2x annualised revenue versus a 603.0x peer median, and Dencun has compressed L1 fees. The dossier's lean is neutral-to-bear, favouring the lower half.

note.name: Ethereum
note.thesis: Price sits at the bottom of its 30-day range after a 16.1% monthly fall. ETH trades at 3071.2x annualised revenue versus a 603.0x peer median, and Dencun has compressed L1 fees. The dossier's lean is neutral-to-bear, favouring the lower half.
note.what: Ethereum is a proof-of-stake smart-contract network. ETH pays gas, secures the chain via staking, and is the collateral and unit of account for most on-chain finance. Users pay ETH for blockspace; validators earn issuance and fees; base fees are burned.

points.text: 30-day fees were $18.52M, annualised $225.29M; revenue was $7.27M, annualised $88.41M. Seven-day fees annualised $419.40M.
FDV/annualised revenue is 3071.2x versus a 603.0x peer median; FDV/annualised fees is 1205.2x versus 217.5x.
Dencun moved rollup data to blobs, L1 fees collapsed and supply grew about 0.18% in 2025.
ETH is $2,222.58, down 16.1% in 30 days and 3.9% in 24 hours. CoinDesk tied the fall to a $6B Binance hack and $1.5B liquidations.
Funding is -0.0361%/8h now, so shorts pay longs, against the 7-day average of +0.0042%/8h. Long/short is 3.30, with 77% of accounts long.

note.supplyHeadline: No scheduled unlocks in next 90 days
note.supplyText: Circulating and total supply are 122.2M; FDV is $271.52B. DefiLlama shows 128.0M unlocked of 128.0M scheduled, no new tokens in the next 90 days and no cliffs. Ethwatch puts staked at 36.2%, ETFs 5.3%, free float 42.8%. Documented schedule excludes ongoing staking inflation.
note.valuationText: ETH's FDV/annualised revenue is 3071.2x versus a 603.0x peer median; FDV/annualised fees is 1205.2x versus 217.5x. Fees are what users pay; revenue is what the protocol keeps. For a monetary and settlement asset fees understate ETH, but the cash-flow multiple is not cheap.
note.usageText: 30-day fees were $18.52M and revenue $7.27M; seven-day fees annualised $419.40M. Staking rewards are supply-side issuance, not user incentives.

catalysts.text: Glamsterdam targeted; no mainnet date formally set.

risks.title: Fees reaccelerate
risks.text: Seven-day annualised fees are already $419.40M versus $225.29M for 30 days; if sustained, fee compression weakens.

risks.title: Funding stays negative
risks.text: Funding is -0.0361%/8h; sustained negative funding means shorts pay longs and can fuel a squeeze.

risks.title: Hack shock fades
risks.text: The Binance hack passes without further DeFi contagion, lifting ETH back above $2,400.

risks.title: ETF flows reverse
risks.text: One-day $88.58M outflow on 26 Oct is not a trend; sustained inflows would improve demand.

note.positioningText: Funding is -0.0361%/8h now versus a 7-day average of +0.0042%/8h; open interest is $5,181M, down 6.3% over 7 days. The long/short account ratio is 3.30, with 77% of accounts long.
note.conclusion: The dossier's lean is neutral-to-bear, and the evidence favours the lower half: price is at the bottom of its 30-day range, valuation is far above the peer median, and Dencun has compressed L1 fees. Negative funding is the main counterpoint. A daily close below $2,223 opens $1,924; reclaiming $2,400 then $2,567 would shift the view.
note.invalidation: Seven-day annualised fees hold above the 30-day annualised pace for two weeks
note.gaps: No 90-day annualised fees; no incentive/points share; no current Foundation/team/investor sale data; no full ETF flow series.
